children.h: 1 · Is it high for this child?

children.text: Read ALP against the lab's range for age and sex — never the adult range. Growth plates keep ALP high through childhood, highest in the pubertal growth spurt.
After a fatty meal, ALP can rise in blood groups O and B (intestinal ALP): repeat fasting if unsure.

children.cond: Within the range for age and sex

children.text: GGT is not made by bone. A raised GGT means the ALP is from the liver.
Read GGT against the lab's range for age: high in young infants, lowest at 1–6 years — below adult values.

children.subtext: Ask the lab for ALP isoenzymes: liver fraction → treat as liver (Isolated GGT); bone fraction → step 3
Bone (or other) source — go to step 3

children.text: Calcium, phosphate, 25-OH vitamin D, PTH, creatinine (First contact).
Examine: wide wrists, bowed legs, rachitic rosary, bone pain, limp, swelling.

children.cond: Fever with bone pain, or refuses to bear weight

pill.text: Emergency department now: infection or leukemia

children.cond: Night bone pain, limp, swelling, a mass or weight loss

pill.text: Today: X-ray, CBC with smear, LDH, uric acid; oncology if a lesion or abnormal smear (expert opinion)
Same day: repeat calcium with magnesium; pediatrician or endocrinology (expert opinion)

children.cond: High calcium, PTH low or normal

pill.text: Same day: endocrinology — think malignancy, immobilization, vitamin D excess (expert opinion)

children.cond: Low vitamin D, high PTH, or signs of rickets

pill.text: Wrist and knee X-rays; treat rickets — pediatrician or endocrinology

children.cond: High creatinine, or signs of thyroid disease

pill.text: Nephrology (bone disease of CKD) or endocrinology (check TSH)

children.text: Transient hyperphosphatasemia (THI): age < 5 years, no bone or liver disease, normal again within about 4 months. Often follows an infection.
ALP is ≥ 5 × ULN in about 70% — even in the thousands. A very high ALP does not argue against THI.

pill.text: Reassure; repeat ALP and GGT in 3–4 months — no imaging

children.cond: Still high at 4 months, child well
children.subtext: About 20% take longer: repeat again; endocrinology if rising or any new finding (expert opinion)

children.text: The pubertal growth spurt explains most. THI also occurs in older children and adults.

pill.text: Repeat ALP and GGT in 3–4 months (expert opinion)
Endocrinology or metabolic bone referral; ALP isoenzymes (expert opinion)

children.text: Low ALP is abnormal. Repeat first: an EDTA or oxalate tube, or hemolysis, falsely lowers ALP.

pill.text: Think acute Wilson disease: INR now; call hepatology / transplant center now

children.cond: Infant with seizures or breathing difficulty

pill.text: Emergency department now: possible severe hypophosphatasia — tell the team ALP is low

children.cond: Infant with rickets and low ALP

pill.text: Same day: endocrinology or metabolic bone — severe hypophosphatasia

children.subtext: Check zinc — ALP needs zinc; a "normal" ALP may hide cholestasis

children.cond: Early loss of baby teeth with the root intact, rickets, poor growth, craniosynostosis

pill.text: Hypophosphatasia: PLP (vitamin B6), ALPL gene — endocrinology or metabolic bone
Repeat with zinc, magnesium and PLP; review drugs (steroids, chemotherapy), nutrition, thyroid, celiac disease; endocrinology if still low
